Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Software Engineering builds the brains of Waymo's fully autonomous driving technology. Our software allows the Waymo Driver to perceive the world around it, make the right decision for every situation, and deliver people safely to their destinations. We think deeply and solve complex technical challenges in areas like robotics, perception, decision-making and deep learning, while collaborating with hardware and systems engineers. If you’re a software engineer or researcher who’s curious and passionate about Level 4 autonomous driving, we'd like to meet you.

We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship!

Conduct ML modeling experiments and prototyping to build state-of-the-art evaluation tools.
Write code within Waymo’s simulator and evaluation systems.
Design statistical experiments to evaluate the efficacy of ML discriminators.
Collaborate across organizations to deliver impact to both onboard teams and downstream safety and simulation technology launch stakeholders.

Enrolled in a graduate program (Master's or PhD)  in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field.

Our goal is to improve the Waymo Driver performance by owning the end-to-end driving behavior for various onroad problems clusters. We work with upstream and the downstream teams on developing the ML models and integrating into the Waymo Driver. We have access to millions of miles of driving data from a diverse set of sensors, enabling engineers like you to (1) develop methods for efficiently and continuously learning from large scale real-world data, to (2) develop models and model training at scale, to (3) analyze real-world behavior and develop systems for handling the complexities of interacting with the real-world, and (4) optimize models for our onboard and offboard hardware.
In this hybrid role, you will report to a Technical Lead Manager.
You will:
Own tasks in the ML Driver, take responsibility for task performance, create ML methods and recipes to scale and improve tasks.
Analyze behavior of ML systems in real-world application, identify issues and root causes, advise or develop short- and long-term solutions.
Develop methods and recipes for distributed fine-tuning enabling multiple developers to simultaneously improve the model, develop methods and recipes to avoid regression against a production system.
Monitor ML systems in production, develop methods for automatically detecting issues or regressions, develop AI-aided analysis and debugging tooling.
Develop and maintain model evaluation recipes and metrics for measuring and improving performance of pre-trained and fine-tuned models
You have:
Bachelors in Computer Science or a similar discipline, or an equivalent amount of deep learning experience
3+ years experience in Machine Learning and/or Computer Vision
Experience with Python or C++
Experience with ML frameworks like PyTorch or JAX
We prefer:
MS or PhD Degree in Machine Learning, Robotics, Computer Science or a similar discipline
Publications at top-tier conferences like CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ICLR, ICML, ICRA, IROS, RSS, NeurIPS, AAAI, IJCV, PAMI

Software Engineering in the Hardware organization is where software meets the physical world. The Waymo Embedded Software Engineering team develops the critical, safety-critical software running at the edge of the Waymo driver, interfacing directly with steering, braking, propulsion, power distribution, and vehicle sensors. You will develop the abstractions and business logic to safely control and manage autonomous vehicles across different vehicle platforms and OEMs. Operating under stringent real-time, deterministic, and fail-operational constraints, the team builds high-reliability onboard firmware and off-vehicle simulation tooling, having a direct and material impact on Waymo's ability to scale safely to more vehicles and cities.

You will:
Develop high-quality vertically-integrated C++ software systems (on-vehicle firmware and off-vehicle simulation/tooling) running at the edge of the Waymo driver.
Contribute directly to the bring-up, validation, and debugging of next-generation compute platforms, peripheral drivers, and hardware-software interfaces for new vehicle platforms.
Write robust unit tests (such as gTest) and Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) simulation fixtures to validate edge-case handling, system robustness, and fault containment.
Analyze field data logs, vehicle telemetry, and simulation results to identify root causes and improve firmware performance.
Participate in cross-functional engineering workflows, design discussions, and code reviews alongside experienced embedded and systems engineers.
You have:
Enrolled in a BS or MS program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field.
Strong programming foundation in C or C++, with a solid understanding of  data structures, pointers, and memory management.
High curiosity, a continuous learning mindset, and the enthusiasm to explore unfamiliar hardware architectures, tools, and codebases.
Demonstrated problem-solving ability, debugging skills, and comfort navigating ambiguity when working with evolving platforms or prototypes.
Familiarity with Linux development environments, command-line tools, and version control systems (e.g., Git).
We prefer:
Embedded Systems and Real-Time Programming: Hands-on experience developing software for microcontrollers (such as ARM Cortex-M or Cortex-R), bare-metal environments, or RTOS with resource-constrained execution.
Hardware Bring-Up and Lab Debugging: Practical experience with board bring-up, hardware-software integration, and lab instrumentation such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and multimeters.
Testing and Quality: Experience with C++ unit testing frameworks like Google Test (gTest) and test-driven development methodologies.
Open Source and Student Team Experience: Active involvement in collegiate engineering teams (such as Formula SAE, Formula Electric, Baja SAE, robotics clubs) or open-source projects demonstrating dedication to crafting high-quality modern C++ software.
Scripting and Tooling: Proficiency in Python for test automation, telemetry data analysis, or build scripting.

You'll transform messy data into useful models and decision\-making tools, collaborate closely with engineering and business development teams, and own projects from start to finish—including scoping, deployment, and monitoring.
   

  

 In Business Development at Millennium, we identify and onboard trading talent and data advantages that drive profitability. We evaluate data vendor solutions and surface novel data points that create early, differentiated signals ahead of competitors. Some work involves delivering reliable, established solutions, while much of it is creative—extracting hidden insights from existing data and discovering new sources.
   

  

 Strong Python skills are required. Hands\-on experience with large language models (LLMs) and their practical applications is a significant plus. We value humility, reliability, clear communication, and collaborative teamwork.

* Own outcomes: break projects into milestones, estimate realistically, meet deadlines, and surface risks early with options.
* Build and deploy models: develop ML models (including LLM\-enabled solutions when appropriate), design features, evaluate rigorously, and contribute to production\-grade pipelines.
* Work the full data lifecycle: wrangle and clean data, implement data quality checks, write maintainable Python/SQL, add tests, and document decisions.
* Collaborate cross\-functionally: translate business questions into analysis, present trade\-offs clearly, and iterate with stakeholders and tech partners.

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, or a related field.
* 3\+ years of hands\-on experience in data science, analytics, or ML, with at least one end\-to\-end project shipped to production used by real stakeholders.
* Strong Python proficiency (Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Scikit\-learn).
* Sound understanding of ML fundamentals: problem framing, validation, metrics, overfitting, feature engineering.
* Experience with SQL and NoSQL database structures along with relational, columnar and document databases.
* Experience with LLMs and modern NLP: prompt engineering, retrieval\-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases, knowledge graphs—plus a pragmatic sense of when not to use them.

* Strong ownership: Plan thoroughly, communicate proactively, and meet deadlines—we value reliability over last\-minute heroics
